correctness.rationale: For a specified k-cycle, the weighted Laplacian minor for forests with k designated roots is the diagonal-minus-rank-one matrix and has determinant (sum_root x) X^(s-1). Setting root weights to one gives occupancy of s nonroot bins under s-1 iid uniform throws into n bins, so the exact inclusion–exclusion/coefficient formula follows. At fixed leaf count r, the coefficient expansion has leading term the displayed fixed-degree polynomial leading term, uniformly for y=k/n in the admissible lattice; multiply by the falling factorial and normalize the resulting Riemann sum to obtain the beta-square distribution. Exactly 455 exact formula comparisons plus 34 independent raw graph-enumeration joint-cell comparisons passed. Finite checks do not prove the asymptotic theorem.

value.rationale: Cycle length and leaf count are two intrinsic graph-shape observables in the canonical connected unicyclic model. Conditioning on few leaves is a natural rare-structure regime; the result supplies exact finite (n,k,r) counts, surprising exact uniformity for one leaf, and a coherent family of Beta(1/2,r) laws for the squared cycle fraction across all fixed r. Its density (1-y^2)^(r-1) explicitly records how the leaf constraint alters global cycle geometry. This is a motivated conditional-law classification, not just a computed table or an unmotivated special graph.
